drivingQuestion: Does 'types of a meal offering' obligate one offering or two?
outcomeNote: the dilemma is taken up in the following units

segments.he: ״מִנְחָה״, ״מִין הַמִּנְחָה״ [וְכוּ׳]. בָּעֵי רַב פָּפָּא: ״מִינֵי מִנְחָה״ מַהוּ?
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that if one says: It is incumbent upon me to bring «a meal offering,» or: It is incumbent upon me to bring «a type of meal offering,» he must bring one meal offering. This is because he stated his intent in the singular. But if he says in the plural: It is incumbent upon me to bring meal offerings, or: Meal offerings of a certain type, he must bring two meal offerings. «Rav Pappa raises a dilemma:» If one said: It is incumbent upon me to bring «types of a meal offering,» using a combination of singular and plural forms, «what is» the halakha?
